title: Le prix du métier  (The Price of the Trade)

segments.t: Late at night, Elise Formet calls Mathias Barneville to deliver major industry news. While confirming that superstar Dany Boon has agreed to sign, Elise confronts Mathias on the cynical maneuvering required to win, forcing him to reflect on the nature of their business. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Allô Mathias? Oui, c'est enfin fait.
Dany Boon va signer chez nous?
Oui, il a accepté notre offre.
C'est une très bonne nouvelle, merci.
Tu n'as pas l'air très ravi.
Je suis fatigué par ces négociations.
Tu n'as jamais honte de manipuler?
Honte de quoi? D'obtenir des contrats?
De manipuler tous nos amis artistes?
C'est notre métier, nous l'avons choisi.
Ce métier détruit nos belles amitiés.
Les affaires demandent de la dureté.
Je t'envoie les contrats signés demain.
D'accord, bonne soirée à toi, Élise.
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Allô Mathias? Oui, c'est enfin fait.
'Hello Mathias? Yes, it is finally done.' Elise delivers the long-awaited news. The telephone greeting 'hello' opens a phone call.
Dany Boon va signer chez nous?
'Is Dany Boon signing with us?' Mathias asks about the star client's signature. The near-future 'va signer' denotes an imminent agreement.
Oui, il a accepté notre offre.
'Yes, he accepted our offer.' Elise confirms the client's consent. The compound past verb 'a accepte' notes formal agreement.
C'est une très bonne nouvelle, merci.
'That is very good news, thank you.' Mathias expresses measured appreciation. The noun phrase 'good' celebrates positive development.
Tu n'as pas l'air très ravi.
'You do not seem very thrilled.' Elise detects a lack of genuine joy. The verbal idiom 'avoir l'air' means to appear or seem.
Je suis fatigué par ces négociations.
'I am tired from these negotiations.' Mathias admits the weariness of endless wrangling. The past participle 'tired' conveys physical and mental strain.
Tu n'as jamais honte de manipuler?
'Are you never ashamed of manipulating?' Elise confronts him with an uncomfortable moral truth. The verbal phrase 'have' means to feel ashamed of.
Honte de quoi? D'obtenir des contrats?
'Ashamed of what? Of getting contracts?' Mathias defends his business results. The infinitive 'to obtain' designates securing tangible outcomes.
De manipuler tous nos amis artistes?
'Of manipulating all our artist friends?' Elise highlights the betrayal of personal relationships. The verb 'to manipulate' denotes using subtle deceit.
C'est notre métier, nous l'avons choisi.
'It is our job, we chose it.' Mathias reminds her of the rules of the agency trade. The compound past 'have' affirms deliberate career choice.
Ce métier détruit nos belles amitiés.
'This profession destroys our good friendships.' Elise mourns the erosion of authentic bonds. The transitive verb 'destroys' conveys destructive damage.
Les affaires demandent de la dureté.
'Business demands toughness.' Mathias explains the uncompromising demands of corporate survival. The noun 'toughness' refers to firmness and emotional resolve.
Je t'envoie les contrats signés demain.
'I will send you signed contracts tomorrow.' Elise returns to immediate paperwork tasks. The present verb 'send' marks prompt document dispatch.
D'accord, bonne soirée à toi, Élise.

'All right, good evening to you, Elise.' Mathias concludes the conversation pensively. The polite closing 'good' wishes a pleasant night. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.
Allô Mathias? Oui, c'est enfin fait.

Je suis fatigué par ces négociations.

C'est notre métier, nous l'avons choisi.

D'accord, bonne soirée à toi, Élise.

Though victorious in securing Dany Boon, Mathias is left alone with the bitter truth of Elise's words. In the cutthroat world of Parisian talent representation, triumph often comes at the price of personal integrity. Now let's listen to the scene one last time in French.
D'accord, bonne soirée à toi, Élise.
